title: Verify data and query results
summary: Define the expected meaning, then check the result using the actual data model and engine.

sections.label: Inputs
sections.text: The requested behavior, permitted data scope, relevant schema or model version, representative fixtures, expected results and the actual query interface and target engine.

sections.label: Procedure
items: Record expected results and scope before choosing checks. Include normal, empty, invalid and unavailable cases where relevant.
Choose checks that fit the data model. SQL tables, RDF graphs and property graphs have different structure and query semantics.
Verify structural rules that actually apply, then compare returned values with the expected result and permitted scope.
Record the dataset, query or API request, engine and version, observed result and limitations. A valid shape does not establish the factual truth of a record.
When performance matters, use supported diagnostics and measured workloads from the target engine. Distinguish a local fixture check from evidence in the target environment.

sections.label: Keep the data families distinct
rows: Which tables, keys, joins, null behavior and transaction boundaries affect the expected result?
Which graph, vocabulary, inference assumptions, shapes and missing statements affect the result?
Which labels, relationships, properties, traversals and engine behavior affect the result?

sections.label: Output
sections.text: A reproducible check record with expected and actual results, input versions, interface, permitted scope and any untested assumptions.

sections.label: Acceptance checks
sections.text: The result matches the recorded expectation for the tested inputs and scope. Engine specific checks are named explicitly. Missing tests remain visible.

sections.label: Specializations
sections.text: The RDF/SPARQL procedure is available below. PostgreSQL, Neptune, Fuseki and Neo4j pages explain different technology examples. Their presence does not imply interchangeable queries or a working integration.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
sections.text: Collect expected versus observed results during Tests and review, and repeat the relevant cases when verifying a repair. Choose checks for the actual data family and engine. The workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Only the source contribution below was verified on 15 October 2026, not every original assertion or project outcome.

sections.label: Gap review: acceptance outputs
items: A check record identifies engine/version, dataset or fixture revision, query or request, permitted scope and expected versus actual values.
Positive, empty, missing or invalid cases have explicit outcomes, with omitted cases marked untested.
Any structural validation report remains separate from source truth, authorization and query behavior evidence.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: W3C SHACL validation takes a data graph and a shapes graph as inputs and produces a validation report. This source contribution applies to the RDF specialization only. It does not define SQL or property graph semantics, prove source truth or validate an untested target engine. Review date: 15 October 2026. This review covers this source contribution only, not the whole guide.

confidence: Moderate. Engine specific checks need local validation

catalog.applicability: Use when verifying a data transformation, query or retrieval API. Select the actual data model and engine before applying specialist checks.
catalog.limits: This is a proposed reading procedure. It does not select an exportable skill, configure access, run checks or establish a successful result.
